page: Microsoft Azure M416s_8_v2 is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine is powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. It features 208 physical cores and 416 dedicated virtual CPUs (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a combined 38 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and hardware AES acceleration. The system allocates 7600.0 GB of system RAM, providing approximately 18.27 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided as a 4398 GB SSD. The configuration includes zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth alongside modest single-core performance. In stress-ng, multi-core CPU performance scored in the top tier at 376,250.84, while single-core performance reached 1,369.48, placing in the bottom quartile. Read-only large block memory bandwidth registered at 746.81 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 339.36 GB/sec, both scoring in the top tier. Parallel decompression using bzip3 achieved 1,473.28 GB/sec in the top tier, whereas single-threaded decompression was limited to 8.68 GB/sec. The PassMark CPU score placed in the top tier at 105,931.2, supported by strong scores in encryption (168,209.61) and extended vector instructions (337,577.94). Network and caching throughput were evidenced by static web serving throughput of 113.81 GB/sec and Redis SET performance reaching 307.64 million operations per second.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the M416s_8_v2 centers on massive scale and high memory consolidation. Because per-core clock speed is standard and single-threaded performance is lower, workloads that rely on single-thread execution latency will yield poor returns on compute investment. Conversely, environments that require massive unified in-memory architectures gain high efficiency by avoiding distributed cross-node networking overheads. The instance is suited for massive in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, large-scale Redis deployments, extensive enterprise data warehousing, and heavily parallelized batch processing pipelines.

It provides an extensive memory capacity of 7600.0 GB (18.27 GB per core) and includes 4398 GB of local SSD storage without bundled GPUs. CPU instruction flags include AVX-512 and AES. Benchmark metrics indicate top-tier parallel execution, including 376,250.84 in stress-ng multi-core and 746.81 GB/sec in large-block uncached read memory bandwidth, alongside high-throughput key-value operations reaching 307.64 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics fall into lower performance tiers. The instance delivers high resource density for workloads demanding extreme memory footprints and parallel multi-threading, including massive in-memory databases, large data caches, and heavy enterprise data transformations.
